deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 106 of the bundle 'HB.Lagrange1816' is a page of German prose in a cursive (Kurrent-style) hand. It continues a narrative of ancient Greek history, apparently lecture or study notes, about the Theban leaders Epaminondas and Pelopidas. It runs on directly from p. 105, where Pelopidas, sent to Thessaly, is imprisoned by Alexander of Pherae and Epaminondas joins the second Theban army as a common soldier. Content of the page:
(1) The Theban army is surrounded by Alexander. In this emergency the soldiers proclaim Epaminondas general again. He beats the tyrant and frees the army and his friend Pelopidas.
(2) Epaminondas now seeks an alliance with Persia and the building of a navy.
(3) In 366 [BC] Pelopidas travels to Susa. He is received with honour and concludes a new alliance with Persia.
(4) A fleet of 100 warships is built.
(5) Soon afterwards a new campaign against Alexander is undertaken, in which Pelopidas dies.
(6) In 364 he marches against Alexander. The battle is as good as won for the Thebans, when heat or rashness leads Pelopidas into a personal attack (continued on p. 107, where he falls). The next page goes on to the Arcadian discord and the 362 BC Mantinea campaign.
No derivation, formula, computation or diagram is present, so there is nothing mathematical to reconstruct. The page looks like a school or university history notebook bound into or misfiled with the Gauss papers. Whether the hand is Gauss's own is doubtful and cannot be decided from this page alone.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Minor historical simplification: in the 368/367 BC episode, Epaminondas mainly extricated the encircled Theban army. Pelopidas was freed in the subsequent campaign largely through pressure and negotiation rather than a decisive battle. 'Der den Tyrannen schlug, die Armee und seinen Freund befreite' compresses these events.
The dates are consistent with the standard chronology: Susa embassy c. 367/366 BC; the naval programme of c. 100 triremes c. 364 BC; Pelopidas' death at Cynoscephalae in 364 BC.

results.modern_name: Not mathematics; standard ancient Greek history (Theban hegemony, 371-362 BC)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine historical lecture notes on Greek history, with no mathematical content. It is of archival interest at most (who wrote it, why it sits in this bundle), not of mathematical-historical significance.

Line 6: the 'auf' marked {+auf+} is written at the end of the line after 'ehrenvoll', with an insertion mark (+) above. The reading 'ehrenvoll auf[genommen]' is plausible ('hier wurde er ehrenvoll auf[genommen]').
Line 7: 'Bündniss' is written with ß/ss ('Bündniß'). The duplicated 'mit' has the first instance struck, as transcribed.

Line 10: the struck word replaced by the marginal 'Alexander' does not clearly read 'Theben'. It may be 'Pherae'/'Pherä' (Alexander of Pherae), which fits the history better. The reading is uncertain.
